First baseline. Modules removed from a bundle by name and re-inlined into it by
an importer, so they are evaluated twice on pages that load both bundles --
with their own state and their own class identities.

THE FLOOR IS SCOPED TO WHAT test_lint.yml INSTALLS, and the number moves with
the install. `-i test_lint` pulls `web` and not `website`, and measures 5 --
all of them in web.assets_frontend_lazy:

  @web/core/browser/cookie   @web/core/utils/dom/ui   @web/public/lazyloader
  @web/public/minimal_dom    @web/session

A wider install legitimately reads higher, and that is not a regression:
`-i website` measures 8, adding @website/js/content/generate_video_iframe and
@website/utils/misc to the same bundle plus @web/../tests/utils in
web.assets_unit_tests; with the test bundles loaded it is 9, the ninth being
@website/interactions/multirange_input in web.assets_frontend. Compare like
with like -- take a control reading at your own scope before believing a local
failure. This is also why the mode is exact=False rather than exact: a lower
reading is a smaller install, not repaid debt. `lint_docstring` is non-exact
for the same reason. It was very nearly floored at 9, which is the reading from
a full install and four units of slack above anything CI can see -- a floor that
could never have fired.

Debt, not a steady state. The one before these was Bootstrap, whose duplicate
gave two EventHandler registries and two Dropdown classes so that NO dropdown on
the website opened; fixed in 0d70ae6d55f by spelling its import
/web/static/lib/... , which esbuild already treats as external.

The five are measured, not inferred: instrumented and loaded in headless
Chrome, web/static/src/session.js logs two evaluations on the website homepage.
They share one cause, and TWO independent constraints block the obvious fix.
Declaring web.assets_frontend_minimal a secondary parent of
web.assets_frontend_lazy stubs every one of them to the shared odoo.loader, and:

1. The stubs need the provider to have run. web.frontend_layout emits the lazy
   bundle's module script BEFORE the minimal one, and module scripts execute in
   document order, so the stubs resolve against an unpopulated loader and
   _makeUser dies on an undefined session: 537 modules registered becomes 12,
   with every response still HTTP 200.

2. Swapping the two to fix that is ALSO wrong, and this is the one that reads as
   working. Only the FIRST ESM bundle's <script type=importmap> is honoured per
   document, and the lazy bundle is the one carrying the web_tour.* dynamic-child
   entries. Measured on the homepage:

     leading with lazy (today)   importmap web.assets_frontend_lazy,    126 entries, 2 web_tour
     leading with minimal        importmap web.assets_frontend_minimal,  22 entries, 0 web_tour

   Ordered that way the page evaluates session.js once and still registers 537
   modules and throws nothing -- the defect is repaired and the browser says so
   -- while every tour has lost the specifiers it resolves through. The tell is
   in the emitted import map, not in the console.
   `enterprise/room/views/room_booking_templates_frontend.xml` states the
   constraint and mirrors the order deliberately; read it before touching this.

So the fix is not ordering, and not ordering plus the declaration. The page's
honoured import map has to carry the lazy bundle's entries while the provider
still runs first -- merging the two maps, or emitting one map per page instead
of one per bundle. That is the bundler change, and it is what closes all five.

Specifiers the secondary-parent mechanism already stubs are subtracted, so a
bundle that is correctly wired reads as clean and the gate can credit its own
fix. Detail:
